issues: Static validation fails because id_event has different enum sets in opening and identity. The opening extraction must use a distinct name or an identical schema.
A neutral collection reply is treated as absence of fresh input. Consecutive non-answers therefore repeat the same question or offer without consuming the applicable persuasion opportunity.
A proposal slot with no amount and no date can become agreement to the full amount today. Contradictory extraction fields can also silently change the customer's act.

A floor offer is marked as used before missing-date clarification finishes. On the next reply, the preserved proposal can be discarded and converted into persuasion. Initial unaffordability also offers the floor today instead of starting individual products at attempt 1 as Brief B requires.
Refusing combined confirmation repeats a correction question indefinitely. Refusals covering several products are processed only for the first product, losing the remaining scope.
Hardship does not consistently suppress persuasion: a saved refusal, rejected floor or rejected calendar offer can call persuade after hardship has been established.

The date parser rejects ordinary spoken birth years, mishandles weekday-plus-ordinal clarification such as 'Friday the thirtieth', and loses useful month or period context. Its amount parser also turns a negative numeric string into a positive amount because clean removes hyphens.

Entity resolution can make a complete credit-card label ambiguous when several cards exist. Confirmation and clarification also need to retain the selected products and unaffected terms instead of resolving against stale negotiation context.
Callback validation waits for both components even when an already supplied day or time is independently outside the permitted window. Rule 7 applies to an invalid day or time.

The identity speaking node combines name confirmation, security, callback and human-request questions while its task describes only security boundaries. These question types need separate initialized speaking stages.

Service-wait handling intercepts human requests before rule 42 can run. A human request immediately before the first final note can also select transfer while finalizing remains true, causing the transfer pre-hook to send an invalid request.
Post-hooks do not reliably normalize a non-object result. An action can retain idle or stale result state instead of producing an authoritative failure instruction.

Several existing checks use a loaded account with zero products, an unreachable state, and omit the consecutive-turn failures above. The supplied evidence is static code inspection only; neither the existing checks nor the proposed checks demonstrate actual dialogue, extraction or platform routing.
